title: GT order-12 Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT (fixed-G2 backport v2)

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in argument.md (compute g=e(P0,Q) via the pinned pairing(Q,P0,True); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate class key and deterministic fruitless-cycle escape; output P=[x]P0 and verify pairing(Q,P,True)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.40 using at most 2^(12589/100) total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents at the fixed C=20000 price in scalar 64-bit AArch64 instruction equivalents, including setup, pairing, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling, cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. Peak memory is below 2^73 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^62 equivalents and is included in the total; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction, 3% explicit step slack, e^-20 detection tail), supported by historical toy-field experiments; no production-size run is claimed. All ledger identities and constants were independently re-derived in exact integer arithmetic; see certificate.json.
